title: Through Jesus’ Blood and Merit
description: Through Jesus’ Blood and Merit in Tonic Solfa to ANGEL'S STORY, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Simon Dach wrote these words in German. August Crull's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 323.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ANGEL'S STORY; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Through Je-sus’ blood and mer-it I am at peace with God; What, then, can daunt my spir-it, How-ev-er dark my road? My cou-rage shall not fail me, For God is on my side; Though hell it-self as-sail me, Its rage I may de-ride.

lines: I am at peace with God;
What, then, can daunt my spirit,
My courage shall not fail me,
For God is on my side;
Me from the love of God;
A sheep for slaughter count me,
Nor things that now are present,
Nor things that are to come,
Shall from the love of God
This child of His and heir.

licence: Public domain: Simon Dach died in 1659; August Crull died in 1923.
credits: Words by Simon Dach (1605–1659), translated by August Crull (1845–1923), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ANGEL'S STORY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
